- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is volatile — and forecasts peak too early; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a sharp spike, model often fails to correct — add a decay factor to recent highs/lows in forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be overly optimistic in early forecast days; consider anchoring to 14-day moving average or recent 7-day range.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with cycle phase — align forecast with sentiment trend direction, not just magnitude.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral, model often drifts toward historical mean — use sentiment as signal to adjust mean reversion strength.
